newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 12.0/13.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 12.0/13.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was stable at 12.0/13.0 percent in late morning on Wednesday.
Dealers said liquidity supply was sufficient, with the central bank supplying 123 billion rupiah earlier.
They said longer-term rates had softened after edging up on Tuesday on tax payment worries for next week. One-week money softened to 12.75 percent from 13.5 percent.
The central bank kept its bilateral rates unchanged.

The central bank offered seven-day bilateral papers (SBIs) at seven percent, two-week at 8.25 percent, one-month at 10.25 percent, three at 10.75 percent, six at 11.25 percent and 12-month at 12.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rates on Tuesday was 12.75 percent, compared with 15.79 percent on Monday.
